source.title: Joint equidistribution of CM points
source.read: arXiv v3 (22 October 2018), the last preprint version, whose comment records that it is to appear in the Annals of Mathematics and was updated following referee comments. Read in the LaTeX source of that version (arXiv e-print of 1710.04557v3, file joint_cm_arxiv_v3.tex, 5208 lines, sha256 of the source archive d76399f101eafbbc52e64185703ddeb820c9e868594feb3316cbe99bb4d5c110), fetched 22 September 2026. The published version in the Annals of Mathematics could not be read here: the article page and its PDF are reachable but no PDF text extraction is available in this environment, so every locator below is a preprint locator and the three source issues are recorded against the preprint with no claim about print. The preprint numbers Theorems, Lemmas, Propositions, Corollaries, Conjectures, Definitions, Examples and Remarks by a single counter running through the whole paper, so that Conjecture 1, Conjecture 2, Theorem 3, Theorem 4, Definition 5, … Proposition 175 are consecutive; there are 175 numbered statements and no duplicate labels. readSections: 1 Introduction (the mixing conjecture of Michel and Venkatesh, summary of results for torus orbits and for Galois orbits, previous results, measure rigidity, cross-correlation, invariants and integral ideals, shifted-convolution sums, further discussion, organization)
2 Preliminaries (notations, forms of PGL_2 and locally homogeneous spaces, the simply connected cover, toral periods, joinings of periodic toral measures)

3 Principal Results (equidistribution of toral orbits, reduction to a fixed invariance group at p_1 and p_2, limit behaviour of the residual spectrum, many-fold toral joinings, Galois orbits of special points)
5 Coordinates for Quaternion Algebras (coordinates over local fields, the different ideal, local maximal orders in coordinates, good integral representatives)
6 The Double Quotient G^Δ\(G × G)/T^Δ (the GIT double quotient, the quotient of G by the adjoint action of T, the quotient of GL_2 by the diagonal torus, descent from GL_{2,E} to B^×)
7 Homogeneous Hecke Sets (Hecke sets containing a joint toral set, volume of a homogeneous Hecke set, equivalence of the necessary conditions for equidistribution)

8 Geometric Expansion of the Pair Cross-Correlation (pair cross-correlation, the main theorem, the geometric expansion, reduction to compact stabilizers, decomposition of the relative orbital integral, archimedean and non-archimedean relative orbital integrals)

9 Sums of Multiplicative Functions along Two-Variable Polynomials (sieving, extending the level of distribution, the sieve bound in a homogeneous arithmetic progression, decoupling multiplicative functions, sums restricted by congruence conditions)
10 Proof of Main Theorem (reduction to a bound on cross-correlation, from a shifted convolution to sums over a polynomial, the sieved upper bound, conclusion)
Appendix: Principal Genus Theory (adelic form of Pic(Λ)/Pic(Λ)², characters orthogonal to Pic(Λ)², 2-torsion in the Picard group)
Appendix: Points on Conics (local diagonalization of binary quadratic forms, regular primes, singular primes)

summary: Khayutin proves the mixing conjecture of Michel and Venkatesh — that the joint packets {(z, σ.z) : z ∈ P} of CM points equidistribute in the product of two modular curves when the minimal norm 𝔑 of an integral ideal in the class of the twist tends to infinity — under two hypotheses: that two fixed primes p_1, p_2 split in every CM field, and that no Dedekind zeta function in the sequence has an exceptional Landau–Siegel zero. He works adelically, with a form G of PGL_2 over Q and self-joinings of periodic toral measures on [(G × G)(A)], and proves that every weak-* limit is (G × G)(A)^+-invariant, a conclusion that cannot be improved because the joint packets may miss connected components; a companion proposition computes exactly which combinations of Haar measures occur. The previous result, of Ellenberg, Michel and Venkatesh, required 𝔑 ≪ |D|^{1/2−η}, which fails for most twists; the new proof removes that restriction by replacing the search for a small Hecke correspondence containing the packet with a direct estimate. The argument has two halves. Measure rigidity, through the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss classification of joinings of higher-rank torus actions, shows that every limit is a convex combination of algebraic measures each of which is either Haar or supported on a homogeneous Hecke set [G^Δ(A)^+ξ]. The second half eliminates the Hecke possibility by bounding the pair cross-correlation of the packet with any Hecke correspondence: unfolding the automorphic kernel gives a geometric expansion into relative orbital integrals indexed by the rational points of the GIT double quotient G^Δ\(G × G)/T^Δ; explicit coordinates for the quaternion algebra split by the CM field turn each orbit into a pair of integral ideals of the quadratic order, with multiplicity bounded by the 2-torsion of the Picard group; and the resulting shifted convolution of ideal-counting functions is a sum along the values of the reduced norm form of the twisting ideal over the lattice points of an ellipse whose eccentricity is controlled by 𝔑. A general two-dimensional sieve, developed from scratch in Section 8, bounds that sum by the expected order with a saving p_1^{-2n} over Bowen balls of the diagonal flow, and the absence of a Siegel zero is used once, to pass from a sum of the ideal-counting function to the class number through L(1, χ_E). The n-fold version and the consequence for Galois orbits of special points on products of quaternionic Shimura varieties follow. In the atlas, GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans lattice-point estimates and the ergodic machinery 'needed for Oppenheim/Duke-type arithmetic applications', AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.1–AA.4 the adelic quotients, reduction theory and strong approximation, HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0 quadratic orders with their Picard groups and ring class fields, SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.0–SV.2 sieve data and the large sieve, AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1 and AN.5 Dirichlet L-functions and multiplicative functions, ShimuraVarieties V4 the reciprocity formula at special points, and the Tau Ceti roadmaps on global number fields and on quadratic form invariants orders, Picard groups and quaternion algebras. Nothing plans joinings, measure rigidity, toral packets, homogeneous Hecke sets, relative orbital integrals for (G^Δ, T^Δ), or the mixing conjecture. Of the 111 items, three are planned and 108 are routed: 73 to a Part II of GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic, 18 as a source of the sieve roadmap, 15 as a source of HE.0, and 2 as a source of AA.4.

items.name: The mixing conjecture of Michel and Venkatesh
items.statement: Let Y be a complex modular curve and let P_i ⊂ Y be a sequence of packets of CM points, each a principal homogeneous space of Pic(Λ_i) for the CM order Λ_i of discriminant D_i < 0. For each i fix σ_i ∈ Pic(Λ_i) and set P_i^joint = {(z, σ_i.z) : z ∈ P_i} ⊂ Y × Y, with μ_i^joint the normalised counting measure on it. Set 𝔑_i = min{Nr(𝔞) : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ_i invertible, 𝔞 ∈ σ_i}. If 𝔑_i → ∞ then μ_i^joint converges weak-* to m_Y × m_Y.
items.note: The conjecture the paper proves under additional hypotheses. Duke's theorem, that the counting measure on a single packet equidistributes when |D_i| → ∞, is the one-fold statement it refines; GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans equidistribution and the ergodic machinery 'needed for Oppenheim/Duke-type arithmetic applications' but names no joint statement.

items.name: Equidistribution of Galois orbits of special points
items.statement: Let X be a finite product of complex modular curves and {x_i} a sequence of special points, i.e. each coordinate is a CM point, with μ_i the normalised counting measure on the finite Galois orbit of x_i. If {x_i} has finite intersection with every proper special subvariety of X, then μ_i converges weak-* to the uniform probability measure on X. This conjecture implies the André–Oort conjecture for products of modular curves, and the mixing conjecture implies a special case of it through the reciprocity map of class field theory.
items.note: The geometric conjecture the mixing conjecture feeds. LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory LD.6 plans o-minimality and unlikely intersections, hence the Pila–Zannier route to André–Oort, but the equidistribution statement is of a different nature and, as the paper notes, the Pila–Zannier strategy sheds no light on it.

items.name: Main theorem for toral packets
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q, K_f < G(A_f) compact open, K_∞ < G(R) a compact real torus, and Y = G(Q)\G(A)/(K_∞ × K_f). Let P_i ⊂ Ỹ be a sequence of K_∞-invariant toral packets with fundamental discriminant D_i < 0, each a principal homogeneous space for an abelian group C_i with a homomorphism C_i → Pic(Λ_i) to the Picard group of the attached order Λ_i in an imaginary quadratic field E_i. Choose σ_i ∈ C_i and let μ_i^joint be the counting measure on {(z, σ_i.z) : z ∈ P_i} ⊂ Y × Y. Fix primes p_1, p_2 and assume for all i that (1) p_1 and p_2 split in E_i, and (2) the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero. If 𝔑_i = min{Nr 𝔞 : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ_i invertible, [𝔞] = [σ_i]} → ∞, then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i^joint} is a convex combination of the uniform probability measures on the connected components of Y × Y.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Theorem 3 of the introduction, a special case of Theorem 14
items.note: The paper's headline theorem: the mixing conjecture under two splitting hypotheses and the absence of a Siegel zero, and with no upper bound on 𝔑_i. The conclusion cannot be improved to equidistribution on all of Y × Y, since the joint packets may miss connected components; Proposition 18 computes exactly which limits occur.

items.name: Main theorem for Galois orbits of special points
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q split over R and let X be a finite product of indefinite Shimura curves relative to G. Let {x_i} be a sequence of special points all of whose coordinates have CM by the same maximal order, with μ_i the counting measure on the Galois orbit of x_i and E_i the CM field. Fix primes p_1, p_2 and assume for all i that p_1, p_2 split in E_i and that the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero. If {x_i} has finite intersection with every proper special subvariety then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i} is a convex combination of the uniform probability measures on the connected components of X.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Theorem 4 of the introduction, restated as Theorem 22
items.note: The geometric consequence, obtained from the n-fold toral theorem through the reciprocity map of class field theory. ShimuraVarieties V4 plans canonical models and the reciprocity formula at special points and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.1 the quaternionic curves; the equidistribution statement is not planned.

items.name: Adelic quotients, anisotropy and the simply connected cover
items.statement: For a linear algebraic group M over Q write [M(A)] = M(Q)\M(A). If M is anisotropic over Q, i.e. has no Q-characters to G_m, then [M(A)] carries a unique M(A)-invariant probability measure. For reductive M, M^sc denotes the simply connected cover, an isogeny M^sc → M is fixed, and M(R)^+ is the image of M^sc(R) for a ring R. For a closed subgroup L < M, L^Δ < M × M is the diagonal, and ctr : M × M → M is (g_1, g_2) ↦ g_1^{-1}g_2.
items.note: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.1 constructs adelic points and their functoriality and AA.3 proves that G(F)\G(A)^1 has finite volume together with the compactness criterion for anisotropic groups; the simply connected cover and the subgroup of images of its rational points are part of the reductive-group package AA.4 uses for strong approximation.

items.name: Forms of PGL_2 and their adelic locally homogeneous spaces
items.statement: Let B be a quaternion algebra over Q, Z the centre of B^×, and G = Z\B^×, a form of PGL_2 over Q; every Q-form of PGL_2 arises this way. Then [G(A)] ≅ Z(A)B^×(Q)\B^×(A). For a compact-open K_f < G(A_f), Ỹ = G(Q)\G(A)/K_f is a finite disjoint union of locally homogeneous spaces Γ_δ\G(R) over δ ∈ G(Q)\G(A_f)/K_f, with Γ_δ = G(Q) ∩ δK_fδ^{-1} a congruence lattice.
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap on quadratic form invariants constructs quaternion algebras with their reduced norm and the split-or-division dichotomy; AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3 supplies the finiteness of G(F)\G(A_f)/K modulo the archimedean connected component that gives the decomposition into locally homogeneous spaces.

items.name: Maximal orders in B and the compact subgroups K_v
items.statement: Fix a maximal Z-order O ⊂ B(Q) with v-adic closures O_v, maximal in B(Q_v); let K_v < G(Q_v) be the image of O_v^×. At a split non-archimedean v the maximal orders are the End_{Z_v}(L) for full-rank lattices L, so K_v is a special maximal compact-open subgroup and O_v^× stabilises a vertex of the Bruhat–Tits tree; at a ramified v the order O_v is unique, O_v^× is normal in B^×(Q_v), and K_v is normal of index 2 in the compact group G(Q_v). At the archimedean place one fixes a maximal compact torus K_∞ < G(R) and the operator norm ‖·‖_∞ attached to the Euclidean norm on R² (or the quaternion norm in the ramified case), with ‖g^{-1}‖_∞ = ‖g‖_∞/|Nrd g|, and sets O_∞ = {‖g‖_∞ ≤ 1}, O_∞^× = {‖g‖_∞ = 1, Nrd g > 0} and Ω̃_∞ = {‖g^{±1}‖_∞ ≤ 2, Nrd g > 0}, a compact symmetric identity neighbourhood on which 1/4 ≤ Nrd ≤ 4.
items.note: The archimedean 'maximal order' is the paper's own device: the closed unit ball of the operator norm is only a multiplicative monoid, not a ring, and it is what makes the archimedean orbital integral of Section 5 finite. The non-archimedean half is standard quaternion arithmetic that no layer of the atlas states in this form.

items.name: The reduced norm and the components of the adelic quotient
items.statement: The reduced norm induces a monomorphism of compact abelian groups Nrd : G(A)/G(A)^+ → A^×/(A^×)², and a monomorphism of double coset spaces G(Q)\G(A)/G(A)^+ → Q^×\A^×/(A^×)². By the Hasse–Schilling–Maass theorem every element of Q^× is a reduced norm when B is split at ∞, and only the positive ones otherwise; so the second map is onto in the split case and has index-2 image otherwise.
items.note: AA.4 plans strong approximation for simply connected almost-simple groups with the required noncompact local factor, which is what identifies G(A)^+ and its class set; the Hasse–Schilling–Maass norm theorem is quaternion arithmetic in the Tau Ceti quadratic-form roadmap's direction.

items.name: Homogeneous toral sets and toral packets
items.statement: For a maximal torus T < G defined and anisotropic over Q and g ∈ G(A), the set [T(A)g] ⊂ [G(A)] is a homogeneous toral set; it carries a T(A)-invariant algebraic probability measure, the periodic toral measure. A toral packet P is the finite collection of orbits in Ỹ of a real torus H < G(R) obtained by projecting a single adelic torus orbit; the set of H-orbits in P is a principal homogeneous space for a finite abelian group C, a quotient of the idele class group of the attached quadratic field E/Q, with a canonical surjection C → Pic(Λ) which is an isomorphism when K_f is maximal.
items.note: The central object, in the sense of Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh. Nothing in the atlas plans toral packets; HE.1 plans CM points on a modular curve as a source of Heegner points, which is the classical special case.

items.name: Local orders attached to a homogeneous toral set
items.statement: With T̃ = E^× for a maximal commutative subalgebra E < B, set Λ_v = E(Q_v) ∩ g_v O_v g_v^{-1} for each place v. For non-archimedean v this is an order in the étale algebra E(Q_v) ≅ E_v; at the archimedean place it is defined by the analogous intersection with O_∞.
items.note: The local invariants of a homogeneous toral set. The Tau Ceti roadmap on global number fields, layer 11, constructs orders in a number field with their conductors and Picard groups, and HE.0 the quadratic orders O_c = Z + cO_K with their ideals; the orders here are cut out by a quaternionic maximal order and an adelic point, which is not that construction.

items.name: The local orders are almost everywhere maximal
items.statement: For almost all non-archimedean v one has Λ_v = O_{E_v}.
items.note: Finiteness of the conductor, which makes the global order of the next item well defined.

items.name: Local structure and Galois stability of the orders
items.statement: For every non-archimedean v there is 𝔣_v ∈ Z_v with Λ_v = Z_v + 𝔣_vO_{E_v}; the conductor of Λ_v is 𝔣_vO_{E_v} and Λ_v is stable under the Galois action of Gal(E_v/Q_v).
items.note: The local form Z_v + 𝔣_vO_{E_v} is the local analogue of the orders O_c = Z + cO_K that HE.0 plans globally; the Galois stability is what makes the coboundary calculus of Section 4 work.

items.name: Local and global discriminants of a homogeneous toral set
items.statement: For non-archimedean v, D_v is the discriminant of the order Λ_v; it equals 1 at every place where E is unramified and Λ_v is maximal. For v archimedean, D_v is defined through the natural topological ring isomorphism with a real quadratic étale algebra, following Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss–Michel–Venkatesh §6.1. The discriminant of the homogeneous toral set is D = ∏_v D_v, a product of disc(Λ) and an archimedean contribution, and it measures the arithmetic complexity of the packet.
items.note: The complexity parameter in every statement of the paper. It is the invariant of Einsiedler, Lindenstrauss, Michel and Venkatesh; the atlas plans discriminants of quadratic orders at HE.0 and in the Tau Ceti orders layer but not the adelic version with its archimedean factor.

items.name: The global order Λ
items.statement: Define Λ = ∩_{v ≠ ∞} Λ_v, the intersection taken inside the 2-dimensional Q-vector space E(Q), an order in E; for all v ≠ ∞ the compact-open subgroup K_{T̃,v} = g_vO_vg_v^{-1} ∩ T̃(Q_v) equals Λ_v^×.
items.note: The global order attached to a homogeneous toral set, of which Pic(Λ) acts on the packet.

items.name: From ideles to ideals
items.statement: Let [T(A)g] be a homogeneous toral set with splitting field E/Q and global order Λ ⊆ O_E. Write Ideals(Λ) for the group of invertible proper Λ-fractional ideals, equivalently the locally principal ones, with the canonical isomorphism to the group of locally principal ideles modulo units, and Ideals(Λ)_0 for the integral ones. The map idl : T̃(A_f) → Ideals(Λ) assigns to an idele the corresponding invertible fractional ideal, and it descends to a map on T(A) with values in Q^×\Ideals(Λ); composing with the class map gives Pic(Λ).
items.note: The dictionary between the adelic twist s ∈ T(A) and an ideal class, which converts the dynamical statement into the arithmetic quantity 𝔑. The Tau Ceti orders layer constructs invertible proper fractional ideals and Pic(O) and warns that not every proper ideal is invertible; the idelic description is HE.0's territory.

items.name: Joinings of periodic toral measures
items.statement: For a maximal torus T < G anisotropic over Q, s ∈ T(A) and g ∈ G(A), the set [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] ⊂ [(G × G)(A)] is a joint homogeneous toral set; the T^Δ(A)-invariant probability measure on it is a self-joining of the periodic toral measure on [T(A)g], since both coordinate projections are that measure.
items.note: The object the main theorem classifies. It is a joining in the sense of ergodic theory, and the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss classification of joinings is one of the inputs.

items.name: The residual quotient G_res
items.statement: Set G_res = G(Q)\G(A)/G(A)^+ and let π^+ : [G(A)] → G_res be the quotient map. The topological space G_res is a compact abelian group and the composite G(A) → [G(A)] → G_res is a continuous surjective group homomorphism.
items.note: The finite abelian quotient through which the connected components of the arithmetic quotient, and the residual spectrum, are seen. AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 plans strong approximation and the level maps that make this quotient finite, but not the quotient itself as a group with its induced measures.

items.name: Classification of limits of joinings of periodic toral measures
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q, K_∞ < G(R) a maximal compact torus and p_1, p_2 finite primes. Let {H_i} be a sequence of joint homogeneous toral sets H_i = [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)], with T maximal anisotropic over Q and splitting field E_i, and let μ_i be the associated joinings. Assume for all i that (1) p_1, p_2 split E_i, (2) the discriminants satisfy |D_i| → ∞, (3) the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero, and (4) the minimal integral norm in the class of the twist tends to infinity. Then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i} is invariant under (G × G)(A)^+, hence a convex combination of Haar measures on the fibres of π^+ × π^+.
items.note: The main adelic theorem, of which Theorem 3 is the geometric shadow. Together with the residual-spectrum proposition it describes the limit points completely.

items.name: Equidistribution against the non-residual spectrum
items.statement: In the setting of the main adelic theorem, for every continuous compactly supported f in the orthogonal complement of the residual spectrum in L²([(G × G)(A)]) one has ∫ f dμ_i → 0.
items.note: The functional form of the main theorem: all the surviving mass is residual.

items.name: Reduction to a fixed invariance group at p_1 and p_2
items.statement: Let {H_i} and {μ_i} be as in the main adelic theorem. Then there is a bounded sequence h_i ∈ G(A) such that H_i(h_i, h_i) ⊆ [(G × G)(A)] satisfies the normalisation conditions at p_1 and p_2; consequently the main theorem for joint homogeneous toral sets satisfying those conditions implies the general case.
items.note: The normalisation that lets the whole argument be run with a fixed compact-open invariance group at the two split primes.

items.name: Limit behaviour of the residual spectrum
items.statement: Let {μ_i} and E_i/Q be as in the main adelic theorem, without assuming its conditions (1)–(4). Assume either that all the fields E_i are distinct, or that they are all equal to a fixed quadratic field E_0. In the first case put H = G_res and in the second the corresponding subgroup attached to E_0. Then the pushforwards (π^+ × π^+)_*μ_i converge to the Haar measure on the corresponding coset of H^Δ; in general they need not converge at all.
items.note: This proposition computes exactly which convex combinations occur in the main theorem, and hence which connected components of Y × Y the joint packets can miss. It is a statement about the residual spectrum of the adelic quotient and about the distribution of the classes of the fields E_i.

items.name: n-fold joint homogeneous toral sets
items.statement: Fix n ∈ N, a maximal torus T < G defined and anisotropic over Q, its diagonal T^Δ < G^{×n}, elements s_1, …, s_{n−1} ∈ T(A) and g ∈ G(A). The set [T^Δ(A)(g, s_1g, …, s_{n−1}g)] ⊂ [G^{×n}(A)] is an n-joint homogeneous toral set.
items.note: The n-fold generalisation of the basic object.

items.name: The n-fold theorem
items.statement: With the same hypotheses as the main adelic theorem, applied to every pair of coordinates, every weak-* limit point of the measures on a sequence of n-joint homogeneous toral sets is (G^{×n})(A)^+-invariant. The deduction from the two-fold case uses the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss joining theorem.
items.note: The n-fold result, which is what feeds the theorem on Galois orbits of special points on a product of n Shimura curves. The Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss joining classification is an external input and is listed as a prerequisite.

items.name: Galois orbits of special points on a product of Shimura curves
items.statement: Let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q split over R, X a product of n quaternionic Shimura varieties relative to G, and {x_i} a sequence of special points all of whose coordinates have CM by the same quadratic order Λ_i < E_i of discriminant D_i < 0 and conductor 𝔣_i. Fix p_1, p_2 and assume for all i the splitting and no-Siegel-zero hypotheses and the finite intersection with proper special subvarieties. Then every weak-* limit point of the counting measures on the Galois orbits is a convex combination of the uniform measures on the connected components of X.
items.note: The geometric theorem, deduced from the n-fold toral theorem by the reciprocity map of class field theory. ShimuraVarieties V4 plans the reciprocity formula at special points and CM.6 the reciprocity exports; the equidistribution statement is new.

items.name: Algebraic measures on adelic quotients
items.statement: Let M be a linear algebraic group over Q. For a finite set S of places containing ∞, a closed finite-index subgroup M < M(Q_S) and a lattice Γ < M, a probability measure ν on Γ\M is algebraic if there is a closed unimodular algebraic subgroup L < M defined and anisotropic over Q and an element g such that ν is the L-invariant measure on a closed orbit. The adelic version is defined by the analogous datum, and a fixed adelic algebraic measure is determined by the G(Q)-orbit of a tuple (L, L′ → L, L, Lg).
items.note: The class of measures the rigidity theorem produces. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans equidistribution and ergodic methods for homogeneous spaces but not the adelic algebraic measures or their classification.

items.name: The split tori A_{p_i} and their positive parts
items.statement: For i ∈ {1,2} let A_{p_i} < G(Q_{p_i}) be the maximal split torus determined by the splitting of E at p_i, and A_{p_i}^+ = A_{p_i} ∩ G(Q_{p_i})^+, the image of a maximal torus of G^sc(Q_{p_i}) isogenous to A_{p_i}, of finite index in A_{p_i}.
items.note: The diagonal flow whose invariance the rigidity theorem produces.

items.name: Measure rigidity for limits of toral joinings
items.statement: Let μ_i^joint be a sequence of self-joinings of periodic toral measures on [(G × G)(A)] with |D_i| → ∞, satisfying the normalisation at p_1, p_2. Then every limit point μ is a convex combination of (A_{p_1}^+ × A_{p_2}^+)^Δ-invariant algebraic measures, described by a probability measure P on the space of such measures; each is either the Haar measure on a fibre of π^+ × π^+ or is supported on a set of the form [G^Δ(A)^+ξ].
items.note: The rigidity half of the proof, deduced from the classification of joinings of Einsiedler and Lindenstrauss together with Linnik's basic lemma and the equidistribution of the torus orbits in each coordinate. This is the statement closest to GN.4's plan for ergodic methods in Duke-type applications, and it is what the cross-correlation estimate is then used to rule out.

items.name: Restriction on the Hecke parameter of a limit
items.statement: If λ is an algebraic measure in the support of P and is supported on [G^Δ(A)^+ξ], then ctr(ξ)_{p_i} ∈ A_{p_i} for i ∈ {1,2}.
items.note: The constraint at the two split primes on the surviving Hecke correspondences.

items.name: Mixing of G(Q_v)^+ on the simply connected adelic quotient
items.statement: For every rational place v that splits B, the action of G(Q_v)^+ is mixing for the Haar measure on [G(A)^+ω_0], for every ω_0 ∈ G(A).
items.note: The mixing input to the ergodic decomposition. GN.4 plans ergodic and mixing proofs for homogeneous spaces; the adelic statement with the simply connected subgroup is the form needed here.

items.name: Ergodic decomposition of a limit joining
items.statement: For P-almost every λ there is ω = (ω_1, ω_2) ∈ G(A) × G(A) such that λ is an (A_{p_1}^+ × A_{p_2}^+)^Δ-invariant measure supported on [(G × G)(A)^+ω], whose projection to each coordinate is the G(A)^+-Haar measure on the corresponding orbit.
items.note: The reduction of the classification to genuine joinings of Haar measures.

items.name: Reduction to an S-arithmetic joining
items.statement: Let λ be as above. Fix a finite set S of places with ∞, p_1, p_2 ∈ S, such that G has class number one with respect to K^S and ω_1, ω_2 ∈ G(Q_S) × K^S. Then λ descends to an S-arithmetic joining, and the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss theorem classifies it: it is the algebraic measure attached to a closed unimodular Q-subgroup L < G × G.
items.note: The step that makes the Einsiedler–Lindenstrauss joining classification applicable.

items.name: The isomorphism type of the joining subgroup
items.statement: In the previous setting the group L is isomorphic either to G or to G × G; and if L < G × G is isomorphic to G and projects onto G in both coordinates then it is conjugate to G^Δ over Q. Moreover one may take L_S = L(Q_S)^+.
items.note: The dichotomy between the trivial joining, which is the Haar measure, and a graph joining supported on a Hecke correspondence. Ruling out the second is exactly what the cross-correlation bound does.

items.name: Coordinates for a quaternion algebra split by E
items.statement: Write M_{2×2} = Spec Q[x_{i,j}] and realise GL_2 by the closed immersion into M_{2×2} × A^1 with coordinate ring Q[x_{i,j}, det^{-1}]. Let Ã be the diagonal torus of GL_2. Fix an isomorphism of E-algebras B_E → M_{2×2,E} carrying T̃_E to Ã_E, and identify B_E = M_{2×2,E} henceforth; the rational structure of B is then given by a twisted Galois action, which differs from the naive entrywise one even when B = M_{2×2}.
items.note: The explicit coordinates in which every local computation of the paper is carried out. The Tau Ceti quadratic-form roadmap constructs quaternion algebras and their splitting criterion; this Galois-descent presentation relative to a fixed maximal subfield and a fixed torus is the paper's own set-up.

items.name: Normal form of the twisting element
items.statement: The twisting element θ has a representative of the form θ = ((0, ε), (1, 0)) with ε ∈ Q^×; every ε ∈ Q^× defines in this way an inner form of M_{2×2} split over E, and the inner forms attached to ε_1, ε_2 are isomorphic over Q if and only if ε_1/ε_2 ∈ Nr(E^×).
items.note: The classification of the forms in these coordinates, by the norm class of ε.

items.name: Rational and local points in coordinates
items.statement: B(Q) = {((a, εb), (^σb, ^σa)) : a, b ∈ E} inside M_{2×2}(E), and likewise B(Q_v) = {((α, εβ), (^σβ, ^σα)) : α, β ∈ E_v} inside M_{2×2}(E_v), the rational points being the matrices with entries in E.
items.note: The explicit description of the points of the form, used in every subsequent computation.

items.name: The different ideal of a local order
items.statement: For v ≠ ∞ define the inverse different of Λ_v ⊂ E_v by Λ̂_v = {a ∈ E_v : Tr(aΛ_v) ⊆ Z_v} and the different by 𝔇(Λ_v) = (Λ_v : Λ̂_v) = {a ∈ Λ_v : aΛ̂_v ⊆ Λ_v}.
items.note: The different of a local quadratic order. The Tau Ceti algebraic-curves roadmap constructs the different for a function field extension and the global number fields roadmap the different of the maximal order; the different of a non-maximal local order, with its relation to the discriminant, is what is needed here.

items.name: The different is principal with norm the discriminant
items.statement: For v ≠ ∞ the different 𝔇(Λ_v) is principal and invertible, and its generator 𝒟_v ∈ Λ_v, well defined up to a unit of Λ_v, satisfies Nr 𝒟_v = D_v.
items.note: The identity that converts the discriminant into an explicit element of the order, used throughout Section 4.

items.name: Local maximal orders at split places
items.statement: For v ≠ ∞ with B(Q_v) split, End_{Z_v}(Λ_v) is the set of matrices ((α, βf), (^σβ/f, ^σα)) with α ∈ Λ̂_v and β − ^σα ∈ Λ_v; more generally there is τ_v ∈ E_v^× with g_vO_vg_v^{-1} the set of ((α, βτ_v), (^σβ/τ_v, ^σα)) with α ∈ Λ̂_v and β − ^σα ∈ Λ_v, equivalently α + β ∈ Λ_v. The element τ_v lies in Λ_v^× for almost all v.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Lemma 44 with Propositions 45 and 47
items.note: The explicit local description of the conjugated maximal order in the chosen coordinates; it is what makes the invariants of Section 7 computable as ideals.

items.name: The archimedean analogue
items.statement: At v = ∞ one has ‖g_∞^{-1}((α, βf), (^σβ/f, ^σα))g_∞‖_∞ = |α| + |β|, so that g_∞Ω̃_∞g_∞^{-1} is described by the corresponding inequalities on |α| and |β|.
items.note: The archimedean counterpart of the local description, which makes the archimedean orbital integral computable.

items.name: Local maximal orders at ramified places
items.statement: If v is inert in E and B(Q_v) is ramified, with ord_v ε = 2k + 1, then g_vO_vg_v^{-1} is the set of ((α, π^{k+1}β), (π^{-k}·^σβ, ^σα)) with α, β ∈ Λ_v. If both E_v/Q_v and B(Q_v) are ramified then, for a uniformiser Π of O_{E_v}, there are u ∈ Z_v^× and k ∈ Z with g_vO_vg_v^{-1} contained in the corresponding set with α, β ∈ Λ̂_v. In general, for any finite v there is τ_v ∈ E_v^× with g_vO_vg_v^{-1} contained in the set of ((α, βυ_vτ_v), (^σβ/τ_v, ^σα)) with α, β ∈ Λ̂_v, where υ_v = 1 if B splits at v.
items.note: The ramified cases of the local description, needed because the quaternion algebra is an arbitrary form.

items.name: Denominators and good integral representatives
items.statement: For a finite place v where G splits let ℬ_v be the Bruhat–Tits building of G(Q_v), and for a ramified v the two-vertex graph G(Q_v)/K_v, with normalised geodesic distance d; the denominator Denom_v(x_v) measures the distance the element x_v moves the base vertex, and Denom_f = ∏_{v ≠ ∞} Denom_v. At the archimedean place the denominator is defined by the operator norm.
items.note: The complexity function on the Hecke correspondences, whose size controls the volume of a homogeneous Hecke set.

items.name: Good integral representatives
items.statement: Let v be a place and x_v ∈ G(Q_v). For every h ∈ Ω_vx_vΩ_v there is r ∈ O_v ⊂ B(Q_v) with h = Z(Q_v)r and |Nrd(r)|_vDenom_v(x_v) = 1 for v ≠ ∞, resp. 2^{-8} ≤ |Nrd(r)|_∞Denom_∞(x_v) ≤ 1 for v = ∞. The same holds with the Bowen balls K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)} in place of Ω_{p_1}.
items.note: The normalisation of representatives of a Hecke element by an integral quaternion of controlled reduced norm; it is what turns the counting problem into a count of integral ideals.

items.name: Bowen balls for the diagonal flow
items.statement: Let B ⊆ G(Q_{p_1}) be an identity neighbourhood, λ a cocharacter spanning X_•(A_{p_1}) and a = λ(p_1). The symmetric homogeneous B-Bowen ball is B^{(−n,n)} = ∩_{k=−n}^{n} a^kBa^{-k}.
items.note: The shrinking neighbourhoods along the diagonal flow in which the correlation is measured.

items.name: The GIT double quotient W
items.statement: Let M = G × T act on the affine variety G × G, the G-coordinate by diagonal left multiplication and the T-coordinate by diagonal right multiplication by the inverse; W denotes the GIT quotient G^Δ\(G × G)/T^Δ. Let w_T ∈ N_G T(Q) be a rational representative of the nontrivial Weyl class; the variety w_TT is well defined even though w_T is not.
items.note: The invariant-theoretic quotient whose points index the terms of the geometric expansion of the cross-correlation.

items.name: Orbits and stabilisers in the double quotient
items.statement: For a rational point γ = (γ_1, γ_2) ∈ (G × G)(Q): the M-orbit of γ is Zariski closed; the stabiliser M_γ is trivial if ctr(γ) = γ_1^{-1}γ_2 ∉ N_GT(Q), and otherwise is the explicit finite or toral group determined by whether ctr(γ) lies in T(Q) or in w_TT(Q).
items.note: The orbit-stabiliser analysis that separates the terms of the geometric expansion into those with compact and non-compact stabilisers.

items.name: The adjoint quotient of G by T and rational separation
items.statement: The natural morphism W → Ad T\G is an isomorphism. Moreover, writing π_W^0 : G → Ad T\G ≅ W for the Ad T-equivariant projection, for γ_0 ∈ G(Q) with γ_0 ∉ w_TT(Q) the rational fibre (π_W^0)^{-1}(γ_0)(Q) is a single Ad T(Q)-orbit.
items.note: The identification of the double quotient with an adjoint quotient, which makes it computable, together with the rational separation statement that makes each term of the geometric expansion a single rational orbit.

items.name: The simply connected torus T^{(1)}
items.statement: G^sc is the group of unit quaternions in B; T^{(1)} is the maximal torus of G^sc over Q mapping to T under the isogeny, namely the unit quaternions in T̃. Likewise A^{(1)} < GL_2 is the rank-one torus of diagonal matrices of determinant 1 and A the split diagonal torus of PGL_2, with A^{(1)} → A surjective as schemes.
items.note: The simply connected tori through which the invariant theory is computed.

items.name: The invariant functions ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ
items.statement: Let A^{(1)} act on M_{2×2} × A^1 by conjugating the matrix and fixing the det^{-1} coordinate; this is equivariant for GL_2 ↪ M_{2×2} × A^1. Define ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ ∈ Q[M_{2×2}] to be, respectively, the two diagonal entries and the product of the off-diagonal entries.
items.note: The explicit generators of the invariant ring.

items.name: The invariant rings
items.statement: Q[M_{2×2} × A^1]^{Ad A^{(1)}} = Q[ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ, det^{-1}], a polynomial algebra; Q[GL_2]^{Ad A^{(1)}} is its quotient by the relation (ϑ_1ϑ_2 − ψ)det^{-1} = 1; and with the grading in which ϑ_1, ϑ_2 have degree 1, ψ degree 2 and det^{-1} degree −2, the ring of Ad A-invariants on PGL_2 is the degree-zero part of the same quotient, generated by ψ det^{-1}, ϑ_1²det^{-1} and ϑ_2²det^{-1}, and isomorphic to Q[x, y, z]/(x² = yz).
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Lemma 65 with Propositions 66, 67 and Corollary 68
items.note: The explicit computation of the invariant ring of the adjoint action of the diagonal torus on PGL_2, which is the local model for the GIT double quotient.

items.name: Galois behaviour of the invariants and descent
items.statement: For g ∈ B^×(Q) ⊂ GL_2(E), or g ∈ B^×(Q_v) ⊂ GL_2(E_v), one has ^σϑ_1(g) = ϑ_2(g), ^σψ(g) = ψ(g) and ^σdet^{-1}(g) = det^{-1}(g). Consequently the image of g ∈ G(Q) in W(Q) is determined by the two values ϑ_1²det^{-1}(g) and ψ det^{-1}(g) in E.
items.note: The descent of the invariant theory from the split form over E to the given Q-form; it is what makes the invariants of the geometric expansion rational.

items.name: Homogeneous Hecke sets
items.statement: For ξ ∈ (G × G)(A), [G^Δ(A)ξ] is a homogeneous Hecke set, carrying a ξ^{-1}G^Δ(A)ξ-invariant algebraic probability measure; [G^Δ(A)^+ξ] is a simply connected homogeneous Hecke set with the analogous measure. The datum defining the set is the class of ξ in G^Δ(Q)\(G × G)(A)/G^Δ(A).
items.note: The Hecke correspondences on which the non-Haar limit measures would be supported; ruling them out is the content of the cross-correlation estimate.

items.name: Hecke sets containing a joint toral set
items.statement: Every homogeneous Hecke set containing [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] is of the form [G^Δ(A)(g, t_Q sg)] for some t_Q ∈ T(Q).
items.note: The parametrisation of the Hecke correspondences that could carry a limit measure.

items.name: The split-place denominator
items.statement: Define the proper continuous function Denom_sf : G(A_f) → N by Denom_sf(h_f) = ∏_{v ≠ ∞ splitting B} Denom_v(h_v); since 1 ≤ Denom_v(ξ_v) ≤ q_v at the finitely many ramified places, Denom_sf ≍_G Denom_f on G(A_f).
items.note: The multiplicative complexity that measures the volume of a Hecke correspondence.

items.name: Volume of a homogeneous Hecke set
items.statement: For ξ ∈ (G × G)(A) with ctr(ξ)_∞ ∈ K_∞ one has vol([G^Δ(A)ξ])·m_G(Ω) = Denom_sf(ctr(ξ)_f)·∏_{p | Denom_sf(ctr(ξ)_f)}(1 + 1/p).
items.note: The exact volume of a Hecke correspondence in terms of its denominator; it is the quantity against which the packet's own volume must be compared, and it is why the method of Ellenberg, Michel and Venkatesh needs 𝔑 ≪ |D|^{1/2−η}.

items.name: The denominator is the minimal ideal norm
items.statement: For τ ∈ T(A) the denominator Denom_f(g_f^{-1}τ_fg_f) is the minimal norm of an integral fractional ideal in the homothety class idl(τ) ∈ Q^×\Ideals(Λ).
items.note: The arithmetic meaning of the denominator: it translates the dynamical complexity of the twist into the arithmetic quantity 𝔑 of the mixing conjecture.

items.name: Equivalence of the necessary conditions for equidistribution
items.statement: For a sequence of joint homogeneous toral sets with global orders Λ_i, twists 𝔰_i = idl(s_{i,f}) and classes [𝔰_i] ∈ Pic(Λ_i), the following are equivalent: the minimal denominator over the Hecke sets containing the packet tends to infinity; the minimal norm of an integral ideal in the class [𝔰_i] tends to infinity; and the corresponding condition on 𝔑_i in the mixing conjecture.
items.note: The proof that the dynamical hypothesis and the arithmetic hypothesis 𝔑_i → ∞ of the mixing conjecture are the same condition, so that the theorem is stated in its natural generality.

items.name: The automorphic kernel and the pair cross-correlation
items.statement: For a compact identity neighbourhood V ⊆ [(G × G)(A)] the automorphic kernel is K_V(x,y) = Σ_{γ ∈ (G×G)(Q)} 1_V(x^{-1}γy). For B = ∏_v B_v ⊆ G(A) a compact identity neighbourhood with B_v = K_v for almost all v and compact open for v finite, probability measures λ_1, λ_2 on [(G × G)(A)] and a closed subset C, the pair cross-correlation Cor_C[λ_1 × λ_2](B) is the integral of K_{B×B} over C × C against λ_1 × λ_2. One always has λ_1 × λ_2({(x,y) ∈ C × C : y ∈ xB}) ≤ Cor_C[λ_1 × λ_2](B), with equality when B is injective on C.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Definitions 80 and 81 with Lemma 82
items.note: The quantity the paper estimates: it measures how much a packet concentrates near a Hecke correspondence, and bounding it is what rules out the non-Haar limits left by the rigidity theorem.

items.name: The ideals attached to a joint toral set
items.statement: For a fixed joint homogeneous toral set [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)]: the twist s defines a homothety class Q^×𝔰 = idl(s) of invertible fractional Λ-ideals; 𝔢 is the invertible fractional ideal attached to the element ε and the local elements υ_v, τ_v of the coordinates of Section 4; and in the simplest case, G ≅ PGL_2 split, one may take ε = 1, υ = 1 and 𝔢 = Λ.
items.note: The arithmetic data entering the shifted-convolution sum.

items.name: The counting functions f_{[𝔤]} and g_{[𝔤]}
items.statement: For [𝔤] ∈ Pic(Λ) define arithmetic functions g_{[𝔤]}(x) = #{𝔞 ∈ Ideals(Λ)_0 : Nr 𝔞 = x, 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, [𝔞] = [𝔤]} and f_{[𝔤]} analogously, counting integral invertible Λ-ideals of a given norm in a given ideal class.
items.note: The multiplicative functions whose shifted convolution the main estimate bounds. They are the ideal-counting functions of a quadratic order; AN.5 plans mean values of multiplicative functions but not these.

items.name: The cross-correlation as a shifted convolution sum
items.statement: Fix a joint homogeneous toral set with splitting field E/Q and quadratic order Λ ≤ O_E of discriminant D, satisfying the normalisation at p_1, p_2. Let B have B_v = Ω_v for v ≠ p_1 and B_{p_1} = K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)}, and fix a simply connected homogeneous Hecke set. Then the cross-correlation is bounded by an explicit constant times a shifted convolution sum of the ideal-counting functions f_{[𝔤]}, g_{[𝔤]} over the values of a binary quadratic form, with the shift determined by the Hecke parameter and the modulus by the ideals 𝔰, 𝔢 and by p_1^{2n}; here υ is supported on primes inert in E while p_1 splits, so gcd(υ, p_1^{2n}) = 1.
items.note: The bridge between the dynamics and analytic number theory, and the technical heart of the paper: the correlation of a toral packet with a Hecke correspondence is a shifted convolution of ideal-counting functions.

items.name: The rational double quotient W_Q and the dagger subgroups
items.statement: Set W_Q = G^Δ(Q)\(G × G)(Q)/T^Δ(Q), with a natural map to W(Q). For a closed subgroup N < M(A) write N^† = N ∩ (G(A)^+ × T(A)), always normal in N.
items.note: The index set of the geometric expansion and the subgroups through which the orbital integrals are taken.

items.name: Geometric expansion of the cross-correlation
items.statement: Let μ be the periodic measure on a joint homogeneous toral set [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] and ν the periodic measure on a simply connected Hecke correspondence [G^Δ(A)^+ξ] with ξ = (ξ_1, ξ_2); set B′ = ξ_1Bg^{-1} × ξ_2Bg^{-1}s^{-1}. Then Cor[μ, ν](B) is the double integral of the automorphic kernel K_{B′} over [G(A)^+] × [T(A)], and unfolding gives a sum of relative orbital integrals indexed by the rational double cosets [γ] ∈ W_Q.
items.note: The unfolding that turns the correlation into a sum over rational orbits, in the manner of a relative trace formula. Nothing in the atlas plans relative orbital integrals for the pair (G^Δ, T^Δ) in G × G.

items.name: Invariance of Haar measure under conjugation on the dagger subgroup
items.statement: For a ∈ M(A), conjugation Ad_a : M(A)^† → M(A)^† preserves any Haar measure on M(A)^†.
items.note: The unimodularity needed for the orbital integrals to be well defined.

items.name: Relative orbital integrals
items.statement: For γ ∈ (G × G)(Q) with M_γ(A) compact, RO_{γ,ϰ}(B) = ∫_{M(A)^†} 1_{B′}((ϰl)^{-1}γt) d(l,t), and the corresponding sum over ϰ in the finite double coset space assembles the contribution of the orbit of γ to the geometric expansion; it splits as a product RO^∞_{γ,ϰ}(B)·RO^f_γ(B) of an archimedean and a non-archimedean factor.
items.note: The local decomposition of the geometric expansion.

items.name: Reduction to compact stabilisers
items.statement: Assume g^{-1}T(Q)sg ∩ B^{-1}ctr(ξ)B = ∅. Then RO_{γ,ϰ}(B) = 0 for every γ with non-compact M_γ(A)^†, and consequently Cor[μ, ν](B) equals the sum over [γ] ∈ W_Q with ψ det^{-1}(γ) ≠ 0 of the corresponding orbital integrals, divided by #M_γ(Q).
items.note: The step that discards the terms with non-compact stabiliser, which would otherwise dominate; the hypothesis is exactly that the Hecke correspondence does not already contain the packet.

items.name: Bound on the non-archimedean orbital integral
items.statement: For [γ] ∈ W_Q, Σ_ϰ RO^f_{γ,ϰ}(B) ≤ 2·m_{G(A_f)}(B_{G,f})·m_{T(A_f)}(B_{T,f})·N_{[γ]}, where N_{[γ]} counts the number of times the M(A_f)-orbit of γ meets B′_f modulo B_{M,f}. This uses that each coset of M(A_f)/B_{M,f} contains at most two cosets of G(Q)M(A_f)^†/B_{M,f}^†.
items.note: The reduction of the non-archimedean orbital integral to a counting problem for the orbits of M on the affine variety G.

items.name: Contraction of the counting function N_{[γ]}
items.statement: Let M = G × T act on the affine variety G with the G-coordinate acting trivially and the T-coordinate by conjugation. The contraction morphism ctr : G × G → G, (g_1, g_2) ↦ g_1^{-1}g_2, is M-equivariant, and the set B′_f is a union of Ad T(A_f)-orbits, so that N_{[γ]} may be computed on the image of the orbit under ctr.
items.note: The reduction of the counting problem to the adjoint quotient, where the invariants of Section 5 apply.

items.name: Bound on the archimedean orbital integral
items.statement: For γ ∈ (G × G)(Q) and ϰ ∈ G(Q) with B_∞ = Ω_∞: RO^∞_{γ,ϰ}(B) = 0 unless ctr(γ) ∈ g_∞Ω_∞ctr(ξ)_∞Ω_∞g_∞^{-1}, and otherwise it is bounded by the product of the volumes of T(R) and of an explicit compact set.
items.note: The archimedean estimate, which is where the compactness of the real torus K_∞ is used.

items.name: The invariant map inv
items.statement: Using the local coordinates of Section 4 one constructs inv_f on Ad K_{T,f}\G(A_f) with values in pairs of homothety classes of integral invertible Λ-ideals, and then inv on the accessible set G(A)_accessible = Ad T(A)G(Q), modulo the adjoint action of T(R) and K_{T,f}, with values in Q^×\(Ideals(Λ)_0 × Ideals(Λ)_0).
items.note: The arithmetic invariant that classifies the orbits appearing in the geometric expansion; it is the paper's replacement for the classical parametrisation of Hecke orbits by ideals.

items.name: The fibres of the invariant map
items.statement: For [h] with inv(h) ∈ Q^×\(Ideals(Λ)_0 × Ideals(Λ)), i.e. h ∉ T(Q), there is a faithful action of ∏_{v ≠ ∞} H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×) on inv^{-1}([h]); consequently #inv^{-1}([h]) ≪ #Pic(Λ)[2].
items.note: The multiplicity bound for the invariant: each pair of ideals is hit boundedly often, by a 2-torsion factor, which is exactly the loss one can afford.

items.name: The ideal classes of the invariants
items.statement: If h = tγt^{-1} with t ∈ T(A) and γ ∈ G(Q), and inv(h) = Q^×(𝔞, 𝔟), then [𝔞] = 1 in Pic(Λ) when 𝔞 ≠ 0, and [𝔟𝔢] ∈ Pic(Λ)² when 𝔟 ≠ 0.
items.note: The constraint on which ideal classes can occur, which is what makes the shifted convolution sum have the shape it does.

items.name: From intersections to invariants
items.statement: Fix (x_v) ∈ G(A_f), with B_v = Ω_v for v ≠ p_1 and B_{p_1} = K_{p_1}^{(−n,n)}. If h ∈ G(A)_accessible lies in ∏_v g_vB_v^{-1}x_vB_vg_v^{-1}s_v^{-1} then inv(h) = Q^×Λ̂(𝔞𝔰^{-1}, 𝔟·^σ𝔰^{-1}) for integral ideals 𝔞, 𝔟 of controlled norms.
items.note: The computation of the invariant of an element of the Hecke set, which produces the two ideals of the shifted convolution.

items.name: The fibre over an integral invariant at an odd ramified prime
items.statement: With inv(h) as above and p | D an odd prime where B splits, the corresponding local cohomology factor acts on the fibre in a way that can be computed explicitly, refining the multiplicity bound.
items.note: The refinement of the multiplicity bound at the primes dividing the discriminant.

items.name: Measure of the Bowen balls at p_1
items.note: The volume computation that turns the Bowen-ball parameter n into the saving p_1^{2n} in the final estimate.

items.name: Solution counts of a binary polynomial
items.statement: For Q ∈ Z[x,y] and a ∈ N let ρ_Q(a) be the number of solutions of Q(x,y) ≡ 0 mod a in (Z/a)², and let X_Q = Spec Z[x,y]/(Q) be the affine plane curve; ρ_Q^sing counts the solutions lying on the singular locus, and ρ̃_Q is the corresponding count of non-singular solutions. For k ∈ N and 0 ≤ l < k, ρ_Q(l; k) is the number of solutions of Q(x,y) ≡ l mod k, so ρ_Q(0; k) = ρ_Q(k) and ρ_Q(l; k) = ρ_{Q−l}(k).
items.note: The local densities of a binary form. SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.0 plans sieve data and local densities in general; these counts for a plane curve, with the singular correction, are the specific input.

items.name: The DeMillo–Lipton–Schwartz–Zippel bound
items.statement: For 0 ≠ Q ∈ Z[x,y] and any prime p not dividing Q, ρ_Q(p) ≤ deg(Q)·p.
items.note: The elementary bound on the number of zeros of a bivariate polynomial modulo a prime. Mathlib has the Schwartz–Zippel lemma for multivariate polynomials over an integral domain, but the statement here is for Z/p with the explicit constant deg(Q).

items.name: Singular and non-singular solution counts
items.statement: For 0 ≠ Q ∈ Z[x,y] and a prime power p^k, ρ̃_Q(p^k) = ρ_Q(p^k) − ρ^sing(p^{k+1})/p².
items.note: The identity separating the singular contribution, which is what allows Hensel lifting to control the higher powers.

items.name: Convex domains of class L(C_l, θ_l) and the class M(A,B,ε)
items.statement: A convex domain E ⊂ R² is C² if its boundary is twice continuously differentiable, with R_max(E) the maximal radius of curvature and A(E) the area; E is of class L(C_l, θ_l) if the number of lattice points in any homothetic copy is controlled by the area with the stated exponent, which by van der Corput holds for every C² convex domain with θ_l = 2/3 + ε. A multiplicative f : N → R is of class M(A,B,ε) if it is non-negative and f(n) ≤ min(A^{Ω(n)}, Bn^ε) for all n > 0.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Definitions 116 and 118 with Remark 117
items.note: The geometric and arithmetic hypotheses of the sieve theorem; the lattice-point count for a convex domain is what GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans, and the class M(A,B,ε) is the divisor-type growth condition.

items.name: A two-dimensional sieve for multiplicative functions along a binary polynomial
items.statement: Let E ⊂ R² be of class L(C_l, θ_l) with R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−3η} for some 1/2 > η > 0, and let Q ∈ Z[x,y] satisfy ρ̃_Q(p^k) ≤ Cp^{k(2−r)} for all prime powers, for some C > 0 and 1 ≥ r > 0. Then, for a multiplicative f of class M(A,B,ε) with ε < r and for X in the admissible range, Σ_{(x,y) ∈ E ∩ Z²} f(Q(x,y)) is bounded by A(E) times the expected Euler product, with an explicit dependence on the parameters.
items.note: The main analytic theorem of the paper: an upper bound of the expected order for the average of a multiplicative function along the values of a binary form over the lattice points of a convex domain, uniform in the domain and the form. It is a general sieve statement and is routed to the sieve roadmap rather than to the dynamical Part II.

items.name: A Mertens-type lower bound
items.statement: Let g : N → R be multiplicative with 0 ≤ g(p) ≤ d for all primes p. Then for any z > 1, Σ_{n ≤ z} μ(n)²g(n)/n ≫_d ∏_{d < p ≤ z}(1 − g(p)/p)^{-1}.
items.note: The standard lower bound for the Selberg sieve weight.

items.name: The large sieve applied to a binary polynomial
items.statement: For Q ∈ Z[x,y] and E of class L(C_l, θ_l), if 1 ≤ z ≤ min((A(E)/R_max^{θ_l})^{1/5}, A(E)^{1/2}) then the number of lattice points of E at which Q has no prime factor below z is ≪ A(E)∏_{deg Q < p ≤ z, p ∤ Q}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²). The exponent 1/5 is far from optimal but any positive exponent suffices.
items.note: The large-sieve input. SieveMethodsAndPrimePatterns SV.2 plans the additive and multiplicative large-sieve inequalities and their duality; this is their application to the values of a binary form on a convex domain.

items.name: Extending the level of distribution
items.statement: For Q ∈ Z[x,y], z ≥ 1 and s > 0, ∏_{deg Q < p ≤ z^{1/s}}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²) ≪_{deg Q} s^{deg Q}∏_{deg Q < p ≤ z, p ∤ Q}(1 − ρ_Q(p)/p²); consequently the previous bound holds for 1 ≤ z ≤ A(E)^{ς_0} whenever R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−η}.
items.note: The step that removes the restrictive range of z from the large-sieve bound.

items.name: The sieve bound in a homogeneous arithmetic progression
items.statement: For Q ∈ Z[x,y] and E of class L(C_l, θ_l) with R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−3η}, and for a, z ∈ N with a ≤ A(E)^η and 1 ≤ z ≤ A(E)^ς, the number of lattice points of E with a | Q(x,y) and Q(x,y)/a free of prime factors below z is bounded by the expected main term, with a variant that removes the gcd condition.
items.note: The sieve bound with a divisibility condition, which is what the shifted convolution needs.

items.name: The auxiliary multiplicative function θ_Q
items.statement: Define θ_Q(p^k) = 1 + 2ρ_Q(p)/p² if p ∤ Q and 1 otherwise, for all k ≥ 1, and write θ_Q = 1 * λ_Q, so that by Möbius inversion λ_Q(n) = μ(n)²2^{ω(n)}ρ_Q(n)/n² when gcd(n, Q) = 1 and 0 otherwise. If f ∈ M(A,B,ε) then fθ_Q ∈ M(A′,B′,ε+ε′) for suitable constants.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Definition 127 with Remark 128 and Corollary 129
items.note: The weight that absorbs the divisor-type losses in the sieve.

items.name: Decoupling multiplicative functions
items.statement: Let g, ψ be non-negative multiplicative functions and h = 1 * ψ. Then for z ≥ 1, Σ_{a ≤ z} g(a)h(a) ≤ 𝔐_z(g, ψ)·Σ_{a ≤ z} g(a), with 𝔐_z(g,ψ) = ∏_{p ≤ z}[1 + Σ_{v=1}^{log z/log p} ψ(p^v)Σ_{j ≥ v} g(p^j)], and an upper bound for 𝔐_z in terms of h.
items.note: The decoupling inequality that separates the divisor weight from the counting function; it is a general statement about multiplicative functions and is the technical heart of the sieve section.

items.name: Averaged sieve bounds and exponential savings
items.statement: For Q with ρ̃_Q(p^k) ≤ Cp^{k(2−r)} and f a non-negative multiplicative function with f(n) < Bn^ε and ε < r: Σ_{a ≤ z} ρ̃_Q(a)f(a)θ_Q(a)/a² ≪ Σ_{a ≤ z} …, and for f of class M(A,B,ε) with ε < r the sum restricted to z^α ≤ a ≤ z with P^+(a) ≤ z^{1/s} is exponentially small in the parameters; likewise the sum restricted to extremely smooth a is ≪ z^{−rα+β}.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Lemmas 132, 133 and 135 with Remark 134
items.note: The three averaging lemmas that give the saving in the final bound, in the smooth, rough and intermediate ranges.

items.name: The sieve with fixed congruence conditions
items.statement: Two refinements of the main sieve theorem: one in which the values are divided by a fixed modulus k_0 under strengthened hypotheses on the domain, and one in which the values are restricted modulo k = k_0k_1k_2 with gcd(k_0, k_2) = 1, all primes dividing k_1 dividing k_2, and a fixed residue l invertible mod k_2.
items.note: The forms of the sieve theorem actually used in the application, where the shifted convolution comes with congruence conditions imposed by the ideals 𝔰 and 𝔢.

items.name: Reduction of the main theorem to a bound on cross-correlation
items.statement: Let H_i = [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] be a sequence of joint homogeneous toral sets satisfying the splitting conditions, with algebraic measures μ_i → μ. If there is a function F on G(A) such that the cross-correlation of μ_i with each Hecke correspondence is o of the corresponding volume, uniformly in the relevant range, then μ gives no mass to any homogeneous Hecke set, and hence, by the rigidity theorem, is a convex combination of Haar measures.
items.note: The logical structure of the proof: rigidity leaves two possibilities, and the cross-correlation bound eliminates the Hecke one.

items.name: From a shifted convolution to a binary quadratic form
items.statement: Fix a Z-basis A, B ∈ E^× of the fractional Λ-ideal 𝔰^{-1} and let q(x,y) = Nr(Ax + By)/Nr(𝔰^{-1}), a primitive integral binary quadratic form of discriminant D. Then the shifted convolution sum of the cross-correlation theorem is a sum of the ideal-counting multiplicative functions along the values of q on the lattice points of an explicit region.
items.note: The identification of the shifted convolution with a sum along a binary quadratic form, which is what makes the two-dimensional sieve applicable. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 and GN.3 plan binary quadratic forms, their reduction and their class theory.

items.name: The ellipse and its curvature
items.statement: Taking q to be the reduced norm form of 𝔰^{-1} and E = {(x,y) : q(x,y) ≤ κ|D|}, the set E is an ellipse centred at the origin with area A(E) = 2πκ√|D| and maximal radius of curvature R_max ≤ √(A(E))·(√|D|/𝔑)^{3/2}, where 𝔑 is the minimal norm of an integral ideal in the class of 𝔰.
items.note: The geometric input: the eccentricity of the ellipse is controlled by 𝔑, so the hypothesis 𝔑 → ∞ of the mixing conjecture is exactly what makes the domain admissible for the sieve. This is the point at which the arithmetic hypothesis becomes a geometric one.

items.name: The ideal-counting multiplicative functions
items.statement: Let f : N → N be the multiplicative function counting integral invertible Λ-ideals of a given norm, f(n) = #{𝔞 ∈ Ideals(Λ) : 𝔞 ⊆ Λ, Nr 𝔞 = n}, and let r_0 be the multiplicative function with r_0(p^k) = 2 when p divides the large part of D and k ≥ 1, and the corresponding values otherwise; these are the functions to which the sieve theorem is applied.
items.note: The arithmetic functions of the final estimate; the hypothesis that there is no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero enters through the size of the class number and hence through the average of f.

items.name: Two elementary local lemmas
items.statement: For a uniformiser π of Z_v, two numbers a, b ∈ Q_v satisfy |a − b|_v ≤ 1 if and only if either a, b ∈ Z_v, or |a|_v = |b|_v = |π|_v^{-n} for some n ∈ Z and a/b ≡ 1 mod π^nZ_v. Together with the description of Λ̂_v this is what makes the local computations of the maximal orders effective.
items.note: An elementary p-adic lemma used repeatedly in Section 4.

items.name: Local invariance groups for the orbital integrals
items.statement: For a compact-open B_f < G(A_f), a homogeneous Hecke set [G^Δ(A)^+(ξ_1, ξ_2)] and a homogeneous toral set [T(A)g], set B_{G,f} = ξ_{1,f}B_fξ_{1,f}^{-1} ∩ ξ_{2,f}B_fξ_{2,f}^{-1}, its positive part B_{G,f}^+, and the corresponding groups B_{T,f} and B_{M,f}; the functions f_{γ,ϰ}(l,t) = 1_{B′_f}((ϰl)^{-1}γt) and f_γ(l,t) = 1_{B′_f}(l^{-1}γt) are then invariant under the appropriate dagger subgroups.
items.note: The bookkeeping of invariance groups under which the non-archimedean orbital integrals are computed.

items.name: Reduction of the final shifted convolution to a congruence average
items.statement: The shifted convolution sum of the cross-correlation theorem, restricted to the lattice points of the ellipse at which υp_1^{2n} divides the value of the form, is bounded by an average over residues m modulo k, with weights w_k, of the sum of (f·r_0)(Q(x,y)/υp_1^{2n}) over the lattice points in the corresponding congruence class. Unlike r, the mean value of r_0 is bounded in terms of η alone, independently of D, which is why its contribution is harmless.
items.note: The step that puts the sum in the shape the sieve theorem accepts.

items.name: Admissible lattice-point exponents and the decomposition of D_small
items.statement: An exponent θ_l > 0 is admissible if there is C_l > 0 such that every ellipse defined by a definite integral binary quadratic form belongs to the class L(C_l, θ_l); van der Corput's bound makes every θ_l > 2/3 admissible and Huxley's bound every θ_l > 131/208. For m ∈ Z/k and i ∈ {0,1,2} put D_i(m) = ∏_{p | D_small, ord_p m = i} p, so that D_small = D_0(m)D_1(m)D_2(m).
items.note: The lattice-point counting exponent for ellipses, which is exactly the classical divisor-problem exponent; GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.4 plans lattice-point estimates for convex bodies, and van der Corput's and Huxley's bounds are the inputs quoted here.

items.name: Applying the sieve to the shifted convolution
items.statement: For m ∈ Z/k with positive weight, an admissible θ_l, 0 < η < 1/2, R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−4η} and υp_1^{2n} ≤ |D|^{η/2}, the congruence-restricted sum of (f·r_0)(Q(x,y)/υp_1^{2n}) over the lattice points of the ellipse is bounded by A(E) times an explicit product of local densities and an Euler product.
items.note: The application of the two-dimensional sieve to the sum produced by the geometric expansion.

items.name: The local density bound for the shifted form
items.statement: For m with positive weight and a ∈ N with gcd(a, D_0(m)D_1(m)) = 1, ρ̃_Q(υp_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a)/(υp_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a)² ≪ |ω|²/(p_1^{2n}D_2(m)²a)·∏_{p|a}(1 + 1/p)·∏_{p|D_2(m)}2(1 − 1/p)·r_1(…), with r_1 ≤ r_0.
items.note: The estimate of the local densities of the shifted form, which produces the saving p_1^{-2n}.

items.name: The logarithmic sums with the local densities
items.statement: Under the same hypotheses, the congruence-restricted sum is bounded by A(E)p_1^{-2n} times the local density at the small part of the discriminant, an Euler product over the remaining primes, and a sum of f(a)/a over a ≤ 2κ|D|.
items.note: The intermediate bound, before the analytic input on L(1, χ_E).

items.name: The analytic number theory input
items.statement: For m with positive weight and 1/2 > η > 0, if C > 0 satisfies L′(1, χ_E)/L(1, χ_E) ≤ C log|D_E| — that is, if the Dedekind zeta function of E has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero — then the product of the Euler factors below 2κ|D|^{1−η} with the sum of f(a)/a over a ≤ 2κ|D| coprime to D_0(m)D_1(m) is ≪_{C,η} L(1, χ_E)·∏_{p|𝔣}(…).
items.note: This is the only place where the no-Siegel-zero hypothesis is used: it converts a sum of the ideal-counting function into the class number through L(1, χ_E), with the constant uniform in D. AnalyticNumberTheory AN.1 plans Dirichlet L-functions with their non-vanishing at 1 and AN.3 density estimates and explicit formulas; the exceptional-zero dichotomy in this quantitative form is what is assumed away.

items.name: The final bound on the shifted convolution
items.statement: For an admissible θ_l, 0 < η < 1/2 with R_max^{θ_l} ≤ A(E)^{1−4η}, υp_1^{2n} ≤ |D|^{η/2} and no exceptional zero, the shifted convolution sum Σ_{0 ≤ x ≤ κ|D|, x ≡ w|D| mod υp_1^{2n}} g_{[𝔰]}(x)f_{[p_1^n𝔰𝔢]^{-1}}((x − ω)/υp_1^{2n}) is bounded by the expected main term divided by p_1^{2n}, with an explicit dependence on the conductor and on η.
items.note: The estimate that completes the proof: the correlation of a packet with any Hecke correspondence is smaller than the trivial bound by a factor p_1^{2n}, which tends to zero as the Bowen balls shrink.

items.name: The adelic form of Pic(Λ)/Pic(Λ)²
items.statement: The adelic norm Nr : A_E^× → A^× and the real adelic character χ_E attached to E/Q by global class field theory descend to a short exact sequence 1 → Pic(Λ)/Pic(Λ)² →^{Nr} Q^×\A^×/R_{>0}∏_vNr(Λ_v^×) →^{χ_E} {±1} → 1.
items.note: Gauss's principal genus theorem in adelic form for an arbitrary quadratic order. The Tau Ceti roadmap on global number fields, layer 11, constructs orders and their Picard groups, and HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0 the ring class fields and Artin maps; genus theory for a non-maximal order in this form is not planned.

items.name: The genus index as a product of local norm indices
items.note: The local computation of the genus index.

items.name: Units of a non-maximal local order
items.statement: If Λ_v < O_{E_v} is non-maximal with conductor 𝔣_vO_{E_v} then 1 + 𝔣_vO_{E_v} ⊆ Λ_v^×, and under reduction modulo 𝔣_v one has Λ_v^× = red^{-1}((red Z)^×) = Z_v^× + 𝔣_vO_{E_v}.
items.note: The explicit description of the local unit group of a non-maximal order.

items.name: Norms of local units
items.statement: For v ≠ ∞ with residue characteristic p: Nr O_{E_v}^× = Z_v^× if E_v/Q_v is unramified, and (Z_v^×)² if it is ramified with p > 2; if p = 2 ramifies then Nr O_{E_v}^× is one of the three index-2 subgroups of Z_2^×. For a non-maximal Λ_v: Nr Λ_v^× = (Z_v^×)² when p > 2, and when p = 2 it is given by an explicit case distinction according to the 2-adic valuation of the conductor and the ramification.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Lemmas 158 and 159 with Corollaries 160 and 161
items.note: The local norm computations that make the genus index explicit, including the dyadic cases.

items.name: Kronecker characters
items.statement: For an odd prime p put p* = (−1)^{(p−1)/2}p ≡ 1 mod 4 and χ_p(n) = (p*/n), the unique non-trivial primitive real Dirichlet character of modulus p; and χ_4(n) = (−4/n), χ_8(n) = (8/n), the primitive real characters of modulus 4 and 8.
items.note: The characters cutting out the genera. Mathlib has the Jacobi and Kronecker symbols and quadratic reciprocity, but the packaging as the primitive real characters attached to a discriminant is what is used here.

items.name: The principal genus theorem
items.statement: For 𝔞 ∈ Ideals(Λ), the class [𝔞] lies in Pic(Λ)² if and only if χ(Nr(𝔞)/gcd(Nr(𝔞), modulus(χ)^∞)) = 1 for every character χ in an explicit list: χ_p for every odd prime p | D, and one of χ_4, χ_8, χ_4χ_8 when 2 | D, the choice depending on the local norm group.
items.note: Gauss's genus theory in the form the paper needs: membership in the principal genus is decided by finitely many Kronecker characters evaluated at the norm. This is what makes the ideal classes of the invariants of Section 7 detectable by congruence conditions.

items.name: Galois cohomology of local unit groups and 2-torsion in Pic(Λ)
items.statement: For v ≠ ∞: H^1(Q_v, O_{E_v}^×) is trivial when E_v/Q_v is unramified and Z/2 when it is ramified. For a non-maximal Λ_v with residue characteristic p, #H^1(𝔊, Λ_v^×) = 2 when p > 2 and 2^{μ_wild} when p = 2; for p > 2 the non-trivial cocycle is represented by −1 ∈ Λ_v^{(1)}.
items.note: The cohomological computation behind the multiplicity bound for the invariant map, and the local description of the 2-torsion of the Picard group of the order.

items.name: Local diagonalisation of a binary quadratic form
items.statement: For any prime p the form q is Z_p-equivalent to q′ with Z_p-coefficients, diagonal q′ = ux² + Ay² with u ∈ Z_p^× when p > 2, or when p = 2 and D ≡ 0 mod 4; and for p = 2 with D ≡ 1 mod 4 to an explicit non-diagonal normal form. Writing A = u_Ap^l with u_A ∈ Z_p^×, the invariants of the form are read off from l and the classes of u and u_A.
items.note: The local normal forms of a binary quadratic form. GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 plans the quadratic local-global theory and GN.3 reduction; the Z_p-normal forms with the dyadic case are the specific input to the local density computation.

items.name: Local densities at regular primes
items.statement: If p ∤ ωD then ρ̃_Q(p^k) = ρ_Q(p^k) = ρ_Q(p)p^{k−1} and ρ_Q(p) = p − (D/p).
items.note: The local density of the shifted form at the primes of good reduction, a Legendre-symbol count.

items.name: Local densities at singular primes
items.statement: For q_0 a homogeneous binary quadratic form over Z_p of an explicit normal type, u_3 ∈ Z_p^× and Q_m = q_0 − u_3p^m, the counts ρ_{Q_m}(p^n) are given by explicit formulas. Consequently, for p | ωD with l = ord_p D and m = ord_p(4ω), the counts ρ_Q(p^n) are computed in terms of an auxiliary quantity ρ_Q^0(p) determined by the parity of l and by Legendre symbols; in particular ρ_Q(p^n) ≤ 16p^{n(2−1/2)} for every prime power, and ρ̃_Q(p^n) is given by explicit formulas in the ranges n ≤ l and n > l.
items.locator: arXiv:1710.04557v3 (22 October 2018), Lemma 171 with Propositions 172 and Corollaries 173, 174
items.note: The local densities at the bad primes. The uniform bound ρ_Q(p^n) ≤ 16p^{n(2−1/2)} is exactly the hypothesis ρ̃_Q(p^k) ≤ Cp^{k(2−r)} of the sieve theorem, with r = 1/2, so this is what makes the sieve applicable to the shifted norm form.

items.name: A genus-theoretic sum modulo p²
items.statement: Fix a prime p exactly dividing D, k ∈ {0,1} and assume p ∤ 4ω. For ε ∈ {±1}, the sum of ρ_Q(p^ka; p²) over the units a modulo p^{2−k} with (a/p) = ε is given by an explicit formula distinguishing the cases k = 0 with χ_p(q) = ±ε and k = 1.
items.note: The evaluation that ties the local densities to the genus character χ_p(q), so that the congruence conditions imposed by the ideal classes of the invariants can be summed. It is where the principal genus theory of the previous appendix meets the sieve.

prerequisites.citation: Manfred Einsiedler and Elon Lindenstrauss, Joinings of higher rank torus actions on homogeneous spaces, Publ. Math. IHÉS 129 (2019), 83–127
prerequisites.why: The classification of joinings of higher-rank diagonalisable actions, quoted as Corollary 1.5. It is the engine of the measure-rigidity half of the proof and the only input that makes the n-fold generalisation possible.

prerequisites.citation: W. Duke, Hyperbolic distribution problems and half-integral weight Maass forms, Invent. Math. 92 (1988), 73–90
prerequisites.why: The equidistribution of a single packet of CM points as |D| → ∞, which is the one-fold statement the mixing conjecture refines and which the paper uses as an input in each coordinate. GN.4 names Duke-type applications as its target but plans no proof.

prerequisites.citation: Henryk Iwaniec, Fourier coefficients of modular forms of half-integral weight, Invent. Math. 87 (1987), 385–401
prerequisites.why: The half-integral-weight bound behind Duke's theorem, together with the subsequent generalisations; it is part of the unconditional input the paper builds on.

prerequisites.citation: Philippe Michel and Akshay Venkatesh, Equidistribution, L-functions and ergodic theory: on some problems of Yu. Linnik, International Congress of Mathematicians Vol. II (2006), 421–457
prerequisites.why: Where the mixing conjecture is formulated, and the survey of Linnik's ergodic method and its relation to subconvexity that the whole subject is organised around.

prerequisites.citation: Jordan S. Ellenberg, Philippe Michel and Akshay Venkatesh, Linnik's ergodic method and the distribution of integer points on spheres, Automorphic representations and L-functions, Tata Inst. Fundam. Res. Stud. Math. 22 (2013), 119–185
prerequisites.why: The previous proof of the mixing conjecture, under a single split prime but with the essential restriction 𝔑_i ≪ |D|^{1/2−η}; their strategy — find a Hecke correspondence of small volume containing the packet and use an effective Linnik method with a spectral gap — is what this paper replaces.

prerequisites.citation: Manfred Einsiedler, Elon Lindenstrauss, Philippe Michel and Akshay Venkatesh, Distribution of periodic torus orbits on homogeneous spaces, Duke Math. J. 148 (2009), 119–174
prerequisites.why: Where homogeneous toral sets and toral packets are introduced, with the discriminant that measures their complexity; the paper's Section 2 is written in that language.

prerequisites.citation: Manfred Einsiedler, Elon Lindenstrauss, Philippe Michel and Akshay Venkatesh, Distribution of periodic torus orbits and Duke's theorem for cubic fields, Ann. of Math. 173 (2011), 815–885
prerequisites.why: The definition of the local discriminants of a homogeneous toral set that the paper adopts verbatim (their §6.1), and the model for the combination of measure rigidity with an arithmetic input.

prerequisites.citation: Ilya Khayutin, Large deviations and effective equidistribution, Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2017, no. 10, 3050–3106
prerequisites.why: The author's earlier work removing the hypothesis on G(R) from the argument of Ellenberg, Michel and Venkatesh; it is the source of several of the quantitative tools and of the treatment of the archimedean place.

prerequisites.citation: Irving Reiner, Maximal Orders, London Mathematical Society Monographs 5, Academic Press (1975)
prerequisites.why: Maximal orders in quaternion algebras: their local structure at split and ramified places, the ramification index 2 of a quaternion division algebra over Q_p, and the Hasse–Schilling–Maass norm theorem, all quoted in Section 2.

prerequisites.citation: J. G. van der Corput, Über Gitterpunkte in der Ebene, Math. Ann. 81 (1920), 1–20
prerequisites.why: The lattice-point bound that makes every exponent θ_l > 2/3 admissible for the class of convex domains used in the sieve; GN.4 plans lattice-point estimates but the exponent is quoted, not proved, here.

prerequisites.citation: M. N. Huxley, Exponential sums and lattice points III, Proc. London Math. Soc. 87 (2003), 591–609
prerequisites.why: The sharper lattice-point exponent 131/208, which the paper records as also admissible; it is not needed for the main theorem but fixes the range in which the sieve operates.

prerequisites.citation: Jonathan Pila, O-minimality and the André–Oort conjecture for C^n, Ann. of Math. 173 (2011), 1779–1840
prerequisites.why: The proof of the André–Oort conjecture for products of modular curves, which the equidistribution conjecture of the introduction implies and which, as the paper notes, the Pila–Zannier strategy does not conversely illuminate.

prerequisites.citation: Shou-Wu Zhang, Equidistribution of CM points on quaternion Shimura varieties, Int. Math. Res. Not. 2005, no. 59, 3657–3689
prerequisites.why: One of the generalisations of Duke's theorem to quaternionic Shimura varieties that the paper takes as its unconditional starting point in each coordinate, alongside Michel's subconvexity route.

routes.title: Geometry of numbers, quadratic forms and homogeneous arithmetic, Part II: joinings of toral packets and the mixing conjecture
routes.brief: Plan the joint equidistribution of CM points: toral packets on adelic quotients of forms of PGL_2, their self-joinings, the measure rigidity that classifies the limits, and the cross-correlation estimate that eliminates the remaining possibility, after Khayutin. The final theorems are his Theorems 3, 4, 14, 21 and 22. Theorem 14, the adelic main theorem: let G be a form of PGL_2 over Q, K_∞ < G(R) a maximal compact torus and p_1, p_2 finite primes; let H_i = [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] be a sequence of joint homogeneous toral sets with splitting fields E_i and discriminants D_i, and μ_i the associated self-joinings of periodic toral measures; assume for every i that p_1 and p_2 split in E_i, that |D_i| → ∞, that the Dedekind zeta function of E_i has no exceptional Landau–Siegel zero, and that the minimal norm of an integral invertible ideal in the class of the twist tends to infinity; then every weak-* limit point of {μ_i} is invariant under (G × G)(A)^+, hence a convex combination of the Haar measures on the fibres of π^+ × π^+, and Proposition 18 computes which combinations occur. Theorem 3 is the corresponding statement for a sequence of toral packets on Y × Y and is the mixing conjecture of Michel and Venkatesh under those hypotheses; Theorem 21 is the n-fold version, and Theorem 22 the consequence for Galois orbits of special points on a product of n quaternionic Shimura varieties. The roadmap must cover: homogeneous toral sets [T(A)g] for a maximal Q-anisotropic torus, their periodic measures, toral packets and their local and global discriminants, the joint sets [T^Δ(A)(g, sg)] and their self-joinings; the residual quotient G_res and the statement that equidistribution can only hold componentwise; measure rigidity — algebraic measures on adelic quotients, mixing of G(Q_v)^+ on the simply connected quotient, the ergodic decomposition, the reduction to an S-arithmetic joining and the dichotomy that a limit is either Haar or supported on a Hecke correspondence; explicit coordinates for a quaternion algebra split by the CM field, with the twisted Galois action, the description of the rational and local points, the different of a local quadratic order and the local maximal orders in those coordinates at split, inert and ramified places, together with the archimedean analogue built from the operator norm; denominators, good integral representatives and Bowen balls for the diagonal flow; the GIT double quotient G^Δ\(G × G)/T^Δ, its orbits and stabilisers, the invariant functions ϑ_1, ϑ_2, ψ and the invariant rings, and the descent of the invariants to the Q-form; homogeneous Hecke sets, their volumes in terms of denominators, and the theorem that the dynamical and the arithmetic necessary conditions for equidistribution agree; the pair cross-correlation and its geometric expansion into relative orbital integrals indexed by rational double cosets, the reduction to compact stabilisers, the archimedean and non-archimedean orbital-integral estimates, and the arithmetic invariant map whose fibres are bounded by the 2-torsion of the Picard group; and finally the assembly: the reduction of the main theorem to a bound on cross-correlation, the identification of the shifted convolution with a sum along a binary quadratic form, the ellipse whose eccentricity is controlled by the minimal ideal norm, and the final bound with its saving p_1^{-2n}.
